# mtncloud_load_balancer_cluster_member (Resource)

One role of a cluster's nodes in a load balancer pool, for example a Kubernetes cluster's workers: every node of that role with an address on the load balancer's network becomes a member, as one group. The console keeps the group in step with the cluster: when it gains or loses nodes of that role, they are added to or removed from the pool. The cluster must be one of yours (or one shared with every tenant) with nodes on the load balancer's network. One per cluster role and pool: the cloud adds and removes a group's members together, so a second port for the same role needs `mtncloud_load_balancer_member` per node.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "mtncloud_cluster" "k8s" {
  name = "k8s-prod"
}

# Every worker of the Kubernetes cluster with an address on the network joins the pool, and the
# pool follows the cluster as workers are added or removed. 30080 is a NodePort on the workers.
resource "mtncloud_load_balancer_cluster_member" "workers" {
  network_id       = mtncloud_network.app.id
  load_balancer_id = mtncloud_load_balancer.web.id
  pool_id          = mtncloud_load_balancer_pool.web.id
  cluster_id       = data.mtncloud_cluster.k8s.id
  role             = "kube-worker"
  port             = 30080
}

output "worker_members" {
  value = mtncloud_load_balancer_cluster_member.workers.members[*].address
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (Number) The cluster's ID, for example `data.mtncloud_cluster.k8s.id`. Changing it replaces the members.
- `load_balancer_id` (String) ID of the load balancer, for example `mtncloud_load_balancer.web.id`. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `network_id` (Number) ID of the MTN Network the load balancer is on, for example `mtncloud_network.app.id`. Your tenant must own it: a network shared with you is read-only. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `pool_id` (String) The pool, for example `mtncloud_load_balancer_pool.web.id`. Changing it replaces the members.
- `port` (Number) The port the nodes listen on, for example a Kubernetes NodePort. Set at create: the cloud can't change it, so a change is refused at plan time.
- `role` (String) The nodes' type: `kube-worker` for a Kubernetes cluster's workers, `kube-master` for its masters. Changing it replaces the members.

### Optional

- `backup` (Boolean) Only send traffic here when every other member is down. Defaults to `false`. Changed in place on each member.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `weight` (Number) Each member's share of the traffic, 0 to 256; 0 sends them none. Defaults to `1`. Changed in place on each member.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<cluster_id>:<role>`.
- `members` (Attributes List) The role's members now, sorted by address. The list follows the cluster as it scales. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--members))

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--members"></a>
### Nested Schema for `members`

Read-Only:

- `address` (String) The node's address.
- `id` (String) Member ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The cluster's ID, then : and the role.
terraform import mtncloud_load_balancer_cluster_member.workers <network_id>/<load_balancer_id>/<pool_id>/<cluster_id>:<role>
```
